items.name: Italian Wedding Soup
ingredients: ⅛ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
1 lb. ground Italian sausage hot, mild, or sweet,
½ cup small pasta I used pearled couscous, $0.41**
steps: Gather the ingredients for your meatballs. I find making the meatballs first helps this recipe go a bit faster! You can also form your meatballs a day in advance, or freeze them for easier use later on.
Mix dry ingredients for meatballs; combine the breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan cheese, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Stir to combine.
Add the Italian sausage, breadcrumb mixture, and egg to a large bowl.
Use your hands or a fork to mix them together until just combined.
Divide and shape the mixture into 20 small meatballs, about 1 Tbsp each. Set the meatballs aside.
Gather ingredients for the soup.
Dice the onion, carrots, and celery, and mince the garlic.
Add the olive oil to a large soup pot and heat over medium. Add the diced vegetables, garlic, and Italian seasoning, cooking until the vegetables have softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the chicken broth to the soup, stir to combine, then place a lid on top and bring it up to a boil.
Once the soup is boiling, add the meatballs to the soup and continue to boil until the meatballs are cooked through (about 10 minutes).

(Optional) If you prefer browned meatballs, you can cook them in a skillet with a little olive oil first over medium heat until browned on the outside, then transfer to the boiling soup to finish cooking at this stage in the recipe.
Add the tiny pasta to the boiling soup and continue to boil until the pasta is tender (about 6 minutes).
Finally, stir in the fresh spinach until wilted. Give the soup a taste and adjust the seasonings to your liking. Top with optional parsley, if using. Serve hot and enjoy!

items.name: Steak au Poivre (Black Pepper Steak)
ingredients: 4 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, divided
2 tablespoons cognac, brandy, white wine, or a splash of white wine vinegar
½ cup crème fraîche or sour cream
steps: Crush the peppercorns. Using a mortar and pestle, coarsely crack the black peppercorns. Alternatively, fold the whole peppercorns into a parchment paper packet, like an envelope, and bash them with a kitchen mallet. You want mostly broken peppercorns, with some whole pieces and some crumble.
Using a peppermill (even on the coarse setting) is likely finer than what you’re after. Ideally, the pepper will have a more varied texture with bigger pieces.

Pepper the steaks. Pat steaks dry with a paper towel. Season each side of the steak liberally with Kosher salt. Then, evenly sprinkle cracked peppercorns all across one side of each steak. Press with your palms to pack the peppercorns in so they stick.

Sear the steaks. In a heavy-bottomed skillet, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat. Working in two batches to avoid crowding the pan, place the steaks in the pan, peppercorn-side up, which maximizes the caramelized flavor and reduces the chance of burning the peppercorns.
Sear steaks for about 3 to 4 minutes, undisturbed, per side, flipping with care so the peppercorn crust can stay intact.

Cook until desired level of doneness: For rare, cook until the internal temperature reaches 120°F, for medium-rare aim for 130°F, medium 140°F, medium-well 150°F, and for well-done 160°F. Transfer the steaks to a plate, cover with foil, and set aside.
The steaks will continue to cook and increase in temperature a few more degrees as they rest, so we recommend removing them from the pan at these temperatures.

Make the pan sauce. In the same skillet, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil and turn the heat down to medium. Toss in the shallots and sauté until translucent and lightly browned, about 2 minutes. Add the cognac to the pan, scraping up all the bits of fond stuck on the bottom of the pan.
Let the cognac come to a light boil for about 1 minute (for the alcohol to evaporate) before adding in the beef stock, creme fraiche, and sprigs of thyme.

Reduce the sauce: Stir and simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens, About 5 or 6 minutes, or until the sauce coats the back of a wooden spoon. Finally, stir in the Dijon mustard. Taste and season with salt if needed.

Finish and serve. To serve, fish out the thyme sprigs and pour the sauce over your cooked steaks, or serve the sauce on the side. If you like, you can slice the steaks, plate them, and then drizzle the sauce on top.

items.name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: 3 lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, quartered if large
¼ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper
steps: Preheat oven to 450°. Toss 3 lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, quartered if large, ¼ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ½ tsp. freshly ground black pepper on a rimmed baking sheet to coat.

Arrange in a single layer and roast, tossing occasionally, until tender and browned, 15–25 minutes. MORE WAYS TO ROAST BRUSSELS SPROUTS: Once you’ve mastered the basics, there are plenty of ways to change things up.

Try frico’ed brussels sprouts with a crispy Parmesan crust; brussels sprouts with warm honey glaze or garlicky balsamic brussels sprouts for a savory-sweet finish; or, for a little heat, make roasted brussels sprouts with gochujang brown butter.

items.name: 7 Day High Protein Diet Meal Plan
Apple Spice Cake
ingredients: 2 Tbsp apple spice mix see above
1 stick unsalted butter browned and cooled,
½ cup neutral oil canola or vegetable,
¼ cup apple juice or cider
2 Granny Smith apples peeled and diced, (about 2 cups) $2.18***
2 Honeycrisp or Fuji apples peeled and diced, (about 2 cups) $3.32***
steps: Gather ingredients for cake and spice mix. Preheat oven to 350℉.
Over medium heat, melt a stick of unsalted butter and keep an eye on it, watching for it to begin browning.
Peel and core apples.

Dice apples into small pieces, about 1-2 cm in size. While you’re preparing the apples, keep an eye on your browning butter, giving it a little swirl in the pan every so often, making sure the butter solids don’t burn.
At the halfway point, your butter will look a bit foamy on top, and the butter solids will start to turn golden yellow.
Combine dry cake ingredients (flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt) and the apple spice mix in a large mixing bowl.

Your butter will be perfectly browned after 5-10 minutes over medium heat. Remove the butter from the heat once it’s golden brown and the foam on top has dissipated. Let it cool for a few minutes, swirling it every now and then to help it cool and keep it from burning from the residual heat.

Combine the wet cake ingredients (eggs, neutral oil, applesauce, apple juice or cider, vanilla extract) and the sugars (brown and granulated white sugar). Add the cooled brown butter and mix to combine.
Little by little, add some of the dry mixture to the wet mixture. With a hand mixer on low, continue to add dry mix and blend until the batter is completely combined.
Then, fold in all of the diced apples.
Spray or butter a 9×13 inch pan.
Pour the apple spice cake mix into the prepared 9×13 pan.
Bake at 350℉ for 45 min or until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted in the center of the cake.
Let the cake completely cool, then top with powdered sugar.

items.name: Cider-Braised Sausage and Lentils
ingredients: 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.)
1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped
3 celery stalks, leaves reserved, finely chopped
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed
½ cup finely chopped parsley, plus leaves for serving
3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard
1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar
steps: Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan.

Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan.

Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

Uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

items.name: Mille-Feuille
ingredients: 2 sheets frozen butter puff pastry , 25cm / 10" squares (185g/6oz each), just thawed (Note 1)
1 ½ tbsp soft icing sugar / powdered sugar
1 cup full fat milk (low-fat works too)
½ cup thickened cream / heavy cream , or other whipping cream
1 vanilla bean , split lengthways and seeds scraped out, or 1 tsp vanilla bean paste (Note 2)
3 egg yolks from large eggs (50 – 55g/2oz each in shell) – see here for using egg whites
½ cup caster sugar / superfine sugar , substitute regular / granulated white sugar
1 tbsp / 15g unsalted butter , cold, cut into small 0.7cm / ¼" cubes
¾ cup thickened cream / heavy cream , or other whipping cream (not double cream)
3 tbsp water , just cold tap water
1 cup soft icing sugar / powdered sugar , sifted
4 tsp full fat milk (low-fat works too)
2 tbsp dark chocolate chips / US: semi-sweet chips (Note 4)
steps: Bake puff pastry pressed between sheets. Spread with vanilla icing, pipe chocolate lines then use a toothpick to make the Mille Feuille pattern. Make custard the usual way – it is extra thick.

Cool then incorporate gelatine and whipped cream – the whipped cream lightens it and the gelatine makes the Mille Feuille sliceable. Pipe between puff pastry layers, chill 6 hours to properly set before slicing.
Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F (160°C fan-forced).
Cut each pastry sheet in half, you’ll use 3 halves and pop the 4th back in the freezer for another day.

Prick and dust – Turn 2 baking trays upside down and cover with a sheet of baking paper / parchment paper (Note 5). Place one puff pastry sheet on one tray and two on the other, spaced out as much as you can. Prick all over with a fork (about 30 pricks on each piece). Dust all over with icing sugar using a sifter.
Weigh down – Cover each pastry with another sheet of baking paper / parchment paper and place another tray on top to keep them from puffing up as they bake.

Bake 30 minutes, swapping and turning the trays halfway through, until deep golden and crisp. (The one with 2 sheets on it might take a few extra minutes). Place them on a wire rack and cool completely.
Trim each puff pastry sheets to make them all the same size using a sharp serrated knife. You can either use a ruler or stack them, using one as the master template.

Infuse milk – Put the milk, cream, vanilla bean seeds and used vanilla bean into a large saucepan (~20 cm/8" wide). Heat over medium heat until just below boiling. Remove from heat, cover, and let sit 10 minutes to steep.

Whisk yolks – In a medium size bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar. It will become like wet sand at first, then will turn liquidy and smooth. Add cornflour and flour, whisk until smooth – it will be like a thick cake batter.
Remove vanilla bean from the milk and use your fingers to squeeze all the milk out into the saucepan. Discard used bean.
Temper eggs – While whisking constantly, slowly pour half the vanilla milk mixture into the yolk bowl. Once combined, pour the mixture into the saucepan with the remaining milk and whisk to combine.
Thicken custard – Return the saucepan on medium heat (or medium low if you have a strong burner).

Whisk constantly – leisurely at first, then more briskly as the mixture starts to heat up at which point it will start to thicken into a thick custard – around 7 to 10 minutes, even longer if using a very low heat to be safe.
If you see lumps like scrambled eggs, move it off the heat straight away and whisk them out vigorously until smooth then return to the stove.

Custard goal thickness – The custard is ready when it is very thick dolloping consistency (see video at 2.20 minutes). You should be able to draw a path across the base of the pan and the pan base stays visible. This custard is thicker than usual so you cannot rely on the "bubble" test.

Finish – Remove from the stove. Whisk in the cold butter cubes until incorporated (the butter must be cold, not room temperature else custard may split). Immediately pour into a large bowl, smooth surface, then cover with cling wrap touching the surface to prevent a skin from forming.
Cool on the counter for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for 45 minutes or until it is cool and firms up to a soft rubber-like consistency. (You can even leave it overnight).
Vanilla icing – In a small bowl, whisk icing sugar, vanilla, and milk until smooth. (Don't make this ahead as it will crust over).

Melted chocolate – Place the chocolate chips in a microwave-safe bowl and melt over (3 × 20-second microwave bursts), stirring between each. Transfer to a small piping bag or zip-lock bag. Snip a 2 mm hole (1/6"). (Only melt chocolate just prior to using to ensure it remains fluid).

Mille Feuille icing pattern (see video at 3.58 minutes and step photos) – Place one piece of puff pastry on a rack set on a tray (to catch drips). Spread evenly with the vanilla icing. Pipe on thin lines of the chocolate icing lengthways, making the lines 1 cm / 0.4" apart.
Working quickly before the chocolate sets, use a toothpick to drag through the lines (1.5 cm / 0.6" apart), alternating one way and then the other, to make the classic mille-feuille pattern.
Fridge 30 minutes – Place in the fridge for at least 30 minutes to let it set. It can stay for longer, until you're ready to assemble.

Bloom gelatine – Place the cold water in a small heatproof bowl and sprinkle the gelatine evenly over the surface. Whisk to combine, then leave for 3 minutes until firm and rubbery (this is called "blooming"). Microwave for 15 seconds until melted (do not boil), then cool for 5 minutes.

Loosen custard – Remove the chilled custard from the fridge, it will have firmed up into a soft rubber. Then use a rubber spatula to soften the custard as best you can, I just sort of smear it. It won't become soft creamy, it will be like a soft mushy paste.

Combine custard and gelatine – Transfer a ¼ of the custard into a large saucepan (~20 cm/8" wide) and warm it over low heat, whisking, until it softens a bit more. It won't become fluid but it will be a very soft paste.

Still on the stove, add gelatine and whisk until smooth, it will be like a thick batter consistency. Whisk in another ¼ of the custard until smooth, then remove from the stove and pour that mixture into the custard bowl. Whisk vigorously until smooth.
Set aside to cool slightly while you whip the cream.

Whisk in whipped cream – Beat the cream using an electric beater or stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment until stiff peaks form (upright peaks). Put a quarter of the cream into the custard, then beat it in with the electric beater. Add remaining cream then beat again until smooth. Congratulations, you've made diplomate cream!

Fridge 20 min only – Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 20 minutes so it firms up enough to pipe, but still creamy enough to scoop. Do not refrigerate longer else the gelatine will make the custard set. If you accidentally do this, gently warm to soften then refrigerate again.

Beat smooth – Remove the diplomate cream from the fridge. It will be like a block of soft rubber. Using an electric beater, beat on high for 30 seconds or until the custard is loosened and smooth. Transfer half the custard into a large piping bag and snip the tip of the bag so you have a 1cm / 0.4" round hole (or use a round nozzle).

Layer 1 – Place one cooked pastry sheet on a cutting board. Pipe lengthways on the pastry sheet – I do 6 rows – to cover all the pastry with diplomate cream, aiming to use all the diplomate cream. Dip an offset spatula in warm water then gently smooth the top.
Layer 2 – Place the second pastry sheet on top, press lightly. Fill the piping bag with the remaining diplomate cream and repeat the piping. Smooth the top again.
Layer 3 – Gently place the iced pastry on top, icing facing up. Use any leftover diplomate cream to pipe along the short edges to fill any gaps in the custard and use the offset spatula to smooth it.
Chill – Refrigerate at least 6 hours to set (I usually refrigerate overnight, to be sure).
Slice – Use a sharp serrated knife to cut into 6 pieces, wiping the blade between each slice. If you can, wait another 30 minutes before eating as the custard is even nicer if it's not fridge-cold!

items.name: Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 large potato (russet or yukon gold, peeled and diced small (8 ounces))
steps: Heat oil in a large deep skillet, over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic and sauté 1 minute. Add cumin, masala and curry powder and mix well, cooking 1 minute.
Place chicken in the pan and season with 1 teaspoon salt.
Add tomatoes, cilantro, coconut milk and water.
Stir all ingredients and cover pan, simmer on medium-low until chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Add potatoes, ½ teaspoon salt and simmer, covered an additional 10 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender. Taste for salt and adjust, as needed.
Reduce water to ½ cup and cook the chicken after step 4 on high pressure for 15 minutes, quick release then add potatoes, high pressure 5 minutes. Let it release naturally.

items.name: Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta
ingredients: 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests)
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces
4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
steps: Cook 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests) in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions.

Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over high. Add 1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and toss to coat evenly.
Spread out into an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until mushrooms are starting to release their liquid, 2–3 minutes (do not be alarmed; there will be a lot).
Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until moisture is almost completely evaporated and edges of mushrooms are starting to brown, 6–8 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-high; add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, tossing often, until garlic is fragrant and golden, 1–2 minutes.

Pour in ¾ cup dry white wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan with a sturdy spatula or flat-edged wooden spoon, and cook until wine is mostly evaporated (you should have about 1 Tbsp. liquid left in pan), about 4 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 4 Tbsp.

unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 2 Tbsp. white miso and stir until melted and combined. Slowly pour in ½ cup heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan; simmer until thickened slightly, 2–3 minutes. Add 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce; season with freshly ground pepper.
Taste and add more salt if needed.

Using tongs, transfer pasta to mushroom mixture and add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Increase heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing constantly and adding ½–1 cup more pasta cooking liquid to reach desired sauce consistency if needed, until pasta is al dente and liquid has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.
Remove pan from heat. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup) to pasta and toss to combine. Season generously with more pepper; taste and season with more salt if needed.
Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan and pepper.

items.name: Pumpkin Cornbread Muffins
ingredients: ¾ cup low-fat milk (or dairy-free milk)
⅔ cup maple syrup (I used sugar-free Wholesome Yum)
2 tablespoons unsalted butter (melted and cooled (plus more for serving if desired))
1 cup all purpose flour (or gluten-free flour mix)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F and spray a 12-cup muffin tin generously with nonstick cooking spray.
Add the pumpkin, milk, maple syrup, eggs, and butter to a medium mixing bowl. Whisk to combine and set aside.
To a large mixing bowl, add the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt, pumpkin spice (if using) and cinnamon. Whisk to combine.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until just combined and no streaks of flour remain. Be careful not to over mix.
Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin tin, dividing the batter equally between the cups.

Bake for 15 to 16 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the center of the muffins comes out clean. Remove from the oven and let cool in the muffin tin for 10 minutes. Remove from the muffin tin and serve warm. Serve with extra butter, if desired.

items.name: Baked Chicken Breast Recipe
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts boneless, skinless (approx. 8 oz each) $7.14*
1 Tbsp granulated sugar optional, (can omit for keto/low-carb) $0.02**
2 tsp smoked paprika or sweet paprika,
½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
½ tsp brown sugar optional (omit for sugar-free/keto) $0.01**
steps: Gather ingredients.

Place the chicken breasts between sheets of plastic wrap or put them inside a gallon-size baggie. Use a meat mallet or rolling pin to pound the thicker ends until each breast is an even ½- to ¾-inch thickness throughout.
In a large bowl, add the pounded chicken, 2 quarts of cold water, 2 Tbsp kosher salt, and 1 Tbsp granulated sugar. You can also brine the chicken breasts in a Gallon size (maybe 2) zip-top bag.
Cover and refrigerate the submerged chicken breasts in the brine for 30 minutes. Do not exceed 45 minutes to prevent the meat texture from breaking down.
Preheat your oven to 425°F. In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and brown sugar (if using).

Remove chicken from the brine, rinse quickly under cold water, and thoroughly pat completely dry with clean paper towels.*** Drizzle the breasts with olive oil, then rub the spice mix evenly over all sides of the chicken.

Arrange seasoned chicken breasts in a single layer in a 9×13-inch baking dish or rimmed baking sheet. Bake uncovered at 425°F for 18-20 minutes, or until an instant-read thermometer registers 160-165°F in the thickest part of each chicken breast.

Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate, loosely tent with aluminum foil, and let rest for 5-10 minutes before cutting. The residual heat will finish bringing the internal temperature to 165°F while locking in all the juices. (see notes)

items.name: BA’s Best Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients: 1½ cups plus 1 Tbsp. (200 g) all-purpose flour (spooning into measuring cups, then leveling)
1¼ tsp. (4 g) Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. (4 g) Morton kosher salt
¾ cup (1½ sticks; 169 g) unsalted butter, divided
6 oz. (170 g) bittersweet chocolate (60%–70% cacao), coarsely chopped, or semisweet chocolate chips
steps: Place racks in upper and lower thirds of oven; preheat to 375°. Whisk 1½ cups plus 1 Tbsp. (200 g) all-purpose flour, 1¼ tsp. (4 g) Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. (4 g) Morton kosher salt, and ¾ tsp. (4 g) baking soda in a small bowl; set flour mixture aside.

Cook ½ cup (1 stick; 113 g) unsalted butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, swirling often and scraping bottom of pan with a heatproof rubber spatula, until butter foams, then browns, about 4 minutes.

Scrape melted butter and any brown bits to a large heatproof mixing bowl and let cool 1 minute. Cut remaining ¼ cup (½ stick; 56 g) unsalted butter into small pieces and add to brown butter (it should start to melt but not foam and sizzle, so test with one piece before adding the rest).

Once butter is melted, add 1 cup (200 g) (packed) dark brown sugar and ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar and whisk, breaking up any clumps, until sugar is incorporated and no lumps remain. Add 1 large egg and 2 large egg yolks and whisk until sugar dissolves and mixture is smooth, about 30 seconds.
Whisk in 2 tsp. vanilla extract. Using rubber spatula, fold reserved dry ingredients into butter mixture just until no dry spots remain, then fold in 6 oz.

(170 g) bittersweet chocolate (60%–70% cacao), coarsely chopped, or semisweet chocolate chips (the cookie dough will be soft but should hold its shape once scooped; if it slumps or oozes after being scooped, stir dough back together several times and let rest 5–10 minutes until scoops hold their shape as the flour hydrates).

Using a 1½-oz. scoop (3 Tbsp.), portion out 16 balls of dough and divide between 2 parchment-paper-lined rimmed baking sheets. Bake cookies, rotating sheets if cookies are browning very unevenly (otherwise, just leave them alone), until deep golden brown and firm around the edges, 8–10 minutes.

Let cool on baking sheets. Do Ahead: Dough balls can be portioned 3 months ahead; freeze on cookie sheets and then transfer to a resealable plastic bag. Bake from frozen, adding 1–2 minutes onto the cook time. Cookies can be baked 3 days ahead. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

items.name: 13 Easy Meatloaf Recipes for Weeknight Dinners
Mussels With Garlicky Miso Broth
ingredients: 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, divided
½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (optional)
1 cup dry sake or dry white wine
Country-style bread or steamed white rice (for serving; optional)
steps: Place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp.

crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high.
Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.
Squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.
Ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

items.name: Maple Bourbon Chicken With Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes
¼ cup plus 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce
1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain
1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated
1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped
steps: Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

items.name: Butternut Pasta With Sausage and Dates
ingredients: 1 medium butternut squash (1½–2 lb.), peeled, halved, seeds removed, cut into 1" pieces (about 6 cups)
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
1 lb. hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
3½ oz. Medjool dates (about 6), pitted, sliced lengthwise ¾" thick
12 oz. short tube pasta (such as rigatoni)
1 Tbsp. (or more) sherry vinegar or balsamic vinegar
steps: Cook 1 medium butternut squash (1½–2 lb.), peeled, halved, seeds removed, cut into 1" pieces (about 6 cups), in a large pot of boiling salted water until very tender, 12–14 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer squash to a medium bowl. Reduce heat to low, cover pot, and leave on burner to keep warm.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Add 1 lb. hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and break up into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, about 3 minutes.
Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until browned all over and just cooked through, 3–4 minutes more. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 3½ oz. Medjool dates (about 6), pitted, sliced lengthwise ¾" thick, in same pan, turning halfway though, until deeply browned, 3–4 minutes. Transfer to plate with sausage; season with salt.

Add remaining 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil to pan. Add 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and reserved squash. Cook, scraping up browned bits and smashing squash with spoon to break up, until lightly browned and broken up into a chunky paste (pieces do not need to be even), about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, return cooking liquid in reserved pot to a boil over high heat. Cook 12 oz. short tube pasta (such as rigatoni) until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions (it will finish cooking in sauce). Drain, reserving 3 cups pasta cooking liquid.
Add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid to squash and break up squash with spoon until a saucy consistency. Add pasta, another 1 cup pasta cooking liquid, and reserved sausage and dates.

Increase heat to medium-high; cook, adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is al dente and coated in sauce, 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. sherry vinegar or balsamic vinegar. Taste pasta and add more vinegar, salt and/or pepper if needed.

items.name: Steak Bites With Spinach Couscous
ingredients: 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling
½ cup finely chopped dill, plus sprigs for serving
steps: Place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat.
Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).
Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium.

Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz.

baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps.
Remove from heat; quickly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.)

Uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

Combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.
Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

items.name: Crockpot Chili
ingredients: 15 oz. can diced tomatoes with juices,
15 oz. can diced tomatoes with green chilies (or Rotel) with juices,
15 oz. can kidney beans drained and rinsed, $0.92**
15 oz. can black beans drained and rinsed, $0.92**
15 oz. can pinto beans drained and rinsed, $0.92**
steps: Gather all ingredients.
Dice the onion and bell pepper and mince the garlic. Drain and rinse the canned beans.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until well browned and no longer pink.
In a small bowl, stir together the chili powder, cumin, cayenne pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar, salt, and black pepper.

Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, tomato paste, and half of the chili seasoning to the skillet with the beef. Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are softened, the tomato paste has darkened slightly, and the spices are fragrant.

Transfer the beef mixture to a 6-quart slow cooker. Add the diced tomatoes (with juices), diced tomatoes with green chilies (or Rotel, with juices), kidney beans, black beans, pinto beans, beef broth, and remaining chili seasoning. Stir well to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 to 8 hours or HIGH for 3 to 4 hours, or until the chili is hot and the flavors have melded.
Stir the chili and taste. Adjust the salt or seasonings as needed before serving. Serve with your favorite toppings and enjoy!

items.name: Greek Lentil Soup (Fakes)
ingredients: 1 ½ cups green or brown lentils
½ cup extra virgin olive oil, divided, plus more to serve
steps: Prepare the lentils. Spread the lentils out on a plate or tray and remove any small stones, debris, and any that are shriveled or discolored. Place them in a colander or sieve and rinse under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes dust and any starchy residue.

Cook the lentils. Place the lentils, bay leaves, and water into a pot. Simmer over low to medium heat, half covered, until the lentils are soft and cooked through, about 20 to 35 minutes, depending on the variety.

Sauté the onions. In a separate pot, add ¼ cup of the olive oil and the onion. Sauté over medium heat until soft and translucent, about 10 minutes. Do not let the onion brown. Add garlic and tomato paste, then sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the paprika, and season with salt and pepper, about ½ teaspoon each.

Combine. Pour the cooked lentils, along with their liquid, into the tomato mixture and stir well. If the broth is very thick, add another cup of water to loosen it. Stir in the oregano and remaining ¼ cup of olive oil. Simmer, partially covered, for an additional 5 minutes, or until thickened somewhat.

Finish and serve. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning; it should be well salted. Serve each bowl with a drizzle of olive oil, a teaspoon of red wine vinegar, and a few Kalamata olives.

items.name: Taco Rice
ingredients: 1 pound 93% lean ground beef or ground turkey
1 cup long grain white rice such as Jasmine or Basmati, rinsed and drained
1 (15-ounce can) black beans, rinsed and drained
⅔ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese or Monterey Jack or pepper Jack, plus additional for serving
Chopped cilantro, sliced green onion, plain Greek yogurt (or sour cream), crushed tortilla chips, and/or avocado for serving
steps: Heat a Dutch oven or similar large, deep skillet over medium-high. Once the skillet is hot, add the oil and let warm for a minute. Add the beef, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, salt, and pepper. Let brown, breaking the meat into crumbles, until fully cooked through. Taste to adjust the seasoning.
Stir in the rice, beef broth, salsa, black beans, and green chiles.

Increase the heat and bring the liquid to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and let cook gently for 15 minutes (If your lid has a steam hole, cover it with foil, or the rice will not cook properly. You want all of the steam trapped.)
Check the rice – most of the liquid should be absorbed and if you take a small bite from the center, the rice should be tender. If not, recover and continue cooking, adding a little water if needed.
Once the rice is tender, remove from the heat, cover, and let rest five minutes (this step is important to make sure your rice is nice and fluffy).
Stir in the cheese. Divide into bowls and top with more cheese, cilantro, green onion, Greek yogurt, avocado, or any other desired toppings.

items.name: Schmaltzy Chicken and Stuffing Skillet
ingredients: 2 lb. skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (about 4 medium)
2 celery stalks, leaves reserved, finely chopped
½ cup unsweetened dried cranberries, plus more for serving
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Season 2 lb. skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (about 4 medium) on both sides with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. Pour 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil into a cold large stainless-steel skillet and swirl to coat bottom of pan.

Arrange chicken, skin side down, in pan and place over medium-high heat. Cook undisturbed, rotating pan around on burner often to promote even browning, until skin is browned and chicken releases easily from pan, 7–10 minutes.
Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet or large plate and arrange skin side up.

Combine 1 large onion, finely chopped, 2 celery stalks, finely chopped, and 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in same pan and cook over medium-high heat, stirring often, until onion is softened and just starting to turn golden, 8–12 minutes. Add one 6-oz.

box instant stuffing mix, ½ cup unsweetened dried cranberries, and 1¼ cups water, then finely grate in zest from 1 lemon and set lemon aside. Mix until stuffing is hydrated. Remove pan from heat and push stuffing to sides to create wells for chicken to rest in.
Nestle thighs, skin side up, into stuffing. Transfer pan to oven and bake until chicken is cooked through and top of stuffing is golden brown and crisp, 45–55 minutes.
Top chicken and stuffing with more dried cranberries and reserved celery leaves. Cut reserved lemon into wedges and serve alongside for squeezing over.

items.name: One Pot Broccoli Chicken Mac and Cheese
ingredients: 500g / 1 lb chicken thigh fillets, skinless and boneless, cut into small bite size pieces
½ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, +50% for flakes)
3 cups milk , full fat best but low fat is fine
2 cups chicken stock / broth , low sodium
¾ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, +50% for flakes)
1 large head of broccoli , broken into florets (or 1 ½ smaller ones)

1 ½ – 2 cups (150 – 200g) cups shredded cheese (cheddar, Monterey Jack, Colby, tasty – not mozzarella, too plain), preferably freshly shredded but I usually use pre-shredded ("3 cheese blend" mozzarella, Colby and parmesan)
2 tbsp parmesan cheese , I use the store bought sandy-type (from fridge not aisle), else finely shred you own (tightly pack the tablespoons)
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C/350°F (160°C fan-forced).
Sauté onion – Melt butter over high heat in a large deep oven-proof skillet (30cm/12" wide), or use a large pot. Add onion and cook for 2 minutes.
Cook chicken – Add the chicken and garlic, and sprinkle the garlic powder, salt and pepper over. Cook, stirring, until the surface of the chicken is sealed.

Creamy sauce – Reduce heat to medium high and add flour. Stir until you no longer see white flour. Pour in the stock and stir until it turns milky from the flour dissolving into the liquid. Add milk, salt and pepper. Turn the heat up to high and stir.
Macaroni and broccoli – Add macaroni, stir, then once you start seeing bubbles, spread the broccoli across the surface.
Bake 20 minutes – Cover with a lid and transfer to the oven. Bake 20 minutes.
Crunchy topping – Meanwhile, mix the Crunchy Topping ingredients together.

Cheese and crunch it! Remove the pan from the oven. Flick to oven grill/broiler on high. Remove lid. Scatter with cheese then gently (but quickly!) stir through. It might look a bit watery still, that's good! It will thicken quickly into a creamy sauce. Smooth surface, then sprinkle with Topping.
Golden topping – Place under the broiler/grill for 3 to 5 minutes, or until top is golden. By this time excess liquid will be absorbed by the pasta and the sauce will be thickened and creamy.
Serve immediately while hot and oozy and creamy!

items.name: Frico'ed Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Line a baking sheet with a nonstick baking mat or a sheet of parchment paper generously coated with nonstick vegetable oil spray. Toss 1½ lb. brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp.

Morton kosher salt, and ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper in a medium bowl to combine. Scatter 4 oz. store-bought grated Parmesan (pre-grated works better here than grating from a block) in an even layer over baking sheet, leaving a ½" border around edges.

Arrange brussels sprouts, cut side down, in a single layer on top, spacing evenly to fill baking sheet. Bake until brussels sprouts are tender and browned and cheese is deep golden, 20–28 minutes. (If the cheese in the very center is browned, it’s done.

) Let cool at least 5 minutes, then break into pieces to serve. (Or place another parchment-lined baking sheet upside down on top; holding together, swiftly turn over, peel away mat, and present cheese side up.)

items.name: Toasted Meringue Hazelnut Blondies
ingredients: ¼ cup (packed; 50 g) light brown sugar
2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Lightly coat a 9x9" pan with nonstick vegetable oil spray. Line pan with parchment paper, leaving overhang on two sides. Toast 2 cups blanched hazelnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown and fragrant, 15–18 minutes. Let sit until cool enough to handle, then coarsely chop; set aside.
Cook 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring often, until butter foams, then browns (do not burn), 7–9 minutes. Remove from heat.

Whisk 2 large eggs, room temperature, 1 large egg yolk, room temperature, 1¼ cups (250 g) granulated sugar, ¼ cup (packed; 50 g) light brown sugar, 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¾ tsp.

instant espresso powder (if using) in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium-high speed until mixture is pale and doubled in volume, 6–9 minutes (mixture will form an unbroken ribbon when whisk is lifted from bowl).
Reduce speed to low and with motor running, gradually pour in brown butter in a thin, continuous stream; beat until incorporated, about 2 minutes.

Remove bowl from mixer and gently fold in 1½ cups (187 g) all-purpose flour with a rubber spatula, scraping down sides and bottom of bowl, until no large, dry streaks of flour remain. Scrape batter into prepared pan; smooth surface.
Top with reserved hazelnuts and press in gently to adhere (surface will be smothered with nuts).

Bake blondie until edges are golden brown and center is just set, 35–45 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let blondie cool in pan. Using parchment paper to help, lift blondie out of pan and transfer to rack.

Meanwhile, combine 3 large egg whites and 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar in the clean bowl of stand mixer and set over a saucepan of just simmering water (make sure bottom of bowl does not touch water). Heat, whisking constantly, until sugar is dissolved and an instant-read thermometer registers 170°.

Fit bowl onto mixer fitted with clean whisk attachment. Beat egg white mixture until thick and glossy and mixture is barely lukewarm, 8–10 minutes. Add 1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt; fold in with a rubber spatula just to combine. Taste meringue and season with more kosher salt if needed

Peel away parchment paper from blondie and transfer to a heatproof platter. Using an offset spatula, spread meringue evenly over blondie, covering from edge to edge. Using a kitchen torch, toast meringue until deep golden brown. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Using a long knife and wiping off with a damp kitchen towel between cuts, slice blondie into 9 squares. Do Ahead: Blondie can be baked 24 hours ahead. Store, loosely covered, at room temperature.

items.name: BA’s Best Bolognese
ingredients: 1 lb. ground beef chuck (20% fat), patted dry
3 oz. thinly sliced pancetta, finely chopped
2 cups (or more) homemade chicken stock or low-sodium chicken broth
1 lb. fresh tagliatelle or pappardelle, or dry rigatoni
2 oz. finely grated Parmesan (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
steps: Pulse 1 medium onion, chopped, 1 celery stalk, chopped, and 1 small carrot, peeled, chopped, in a food processor until very finely chopped. Transfer to a small bowl.

Heat 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a Dutch oven or other large pot over medium. Break 1 lb. ground beef chuck (20% fat), patted dry, into small clumps (about 1½") and add to pot; season lightly with kosher salt.

Cook, stirring occasionally but not breaking meat apart, until beef is lightly browned but not crisp, 6–8 minutes. It may be gray in spots (that’s okay!) and still a little pink in the center. Using a slotted spoon, transfer beef to a medium bowl.

Wipe out pot. Cook 3 oz. thinly sliced pancetta, finely chopped, in same pot over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until pancetta has released some of its fat and is crisp, 6–8 minutes. Add reserved vegetable mixture to pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are very soft and beginning to stick to surface, 6–8 minutes.

Return beef to pot and pour in 1 cup dry white wine. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, smashing beef with a wooden spoon, until wine is evaporated, surface of pot is almost dry, and meat is finely ground, 12–15 minutes. (The meat should be reduced to what looks like little bits.

It takes a bit of effort, but you can take breaks.) Add ⅓ cup tomato paste, 1 bay leaf, and one pinch of finely grated nutmeg and cook, stirring occasionally and still pressing down on meat, until tomato paste is slightly darkened, about 5 minutes.

Pour 2 cups chicken stock or broth and 1 cup whole milk into pot; add a pinch of kosher salt. Reduce heat to maintain a very gentle simmer and cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until meat is very, very tender, 2–2½ hours. There shouldn’t be any rapid bubbles at this stage.

Instead, the sauce should release the occasional small bubble or two. When finished, the pasta sauce should have the texture of and look like a sloppy joe mixture. If the liquid reduces before the meat is completely tender, add an extra ½ cup stock and continue cooking. Discard bay leaf.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with salt; keep warm.

Cook 1 lb. fresh tagliatelle or pappardelle, or dry rigatoni, in a large pot of boiling salted water. If using fresh pasta, cook about 3 minutes. If using dry, cook until very al dente, about 2 minutes less than package directions.

Using tongs, transfer cooked pasta to pot with sauce. Add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid and 2 oz. finely grated Parmesan cheese (about ½ cup). Increase heat to medium, bring to a simmer, and cook, tossing constantly, until pasta is al dente and liquid is slightly thickened, about 2 minutes.

Transfer pasta to a platter and top with more Parmesan cheese. Do Ahead: Sauce can be made 4 days ahead. Cover and chill. Editor’s note: This Bolognese sauce recipe was first printed in our January 2019 issue; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our best pasta recipes →

items.name: How Long to Cook a Turkey
Coconut Curry Beans and Greens
ingredients: ¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
2 tsp fresh ginger peeled and grated, (1-inch)
2 15.5 oz. cans cannellini beans drained and rinsed,
13.5 fl oz. can full fat coconut milk
1 lime juiced and zested, (2 Tbsp juice)
½ cup frozen spinach rinsed and squeezed, $1.00****
½ lb. extra firm tofu half a 1lb. block,
steps: Gather ingredients.
Dice onion and bell peppers.
Dice extra firm tofu into small cubes. I didn’t bother pressing it for this recipe.
Rinse and strain beans.
Zest lime, dice carrot, mince garlic, grate ginger, and pick cilantro leaves.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and add olive oil, onion, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, carrots, salt, and pepper. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add garlic, grated ginger, soy sauce, and curry paste. Mix to combine and cook another 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add spinach, lime zest, lime juice, tofu cubes, and white beans.
Stir and add vegetable broth and coconut milk. Simmer on low for 8-10 minutes.
Add cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning to your preferences.

items.name: Pan de Cristal (Glass Bread)
steps: Activate the yeast. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in ¼ cup (60ml) of the water. Set aside.

Knead the dough. To the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook attachment, add all of the flour and 1 ¼ cups (300ml) of the water. Mix with a spatula until no dry spots of flour remain. Knead on medium speed for 5 minutes. Stop the mixer and allow the dough to rest for 5 minutes.

Add the yeast. Pour in the yeast mixture and the salt. Start the mixer on low, and, to avoid splashing, gradually increase the speed to medium-high. The dough may split, but it will soon come back together. Continue kneading on medium-high speed for 5 minutes. Stop the mixer and allow the dough to rest for 5 minutes.

Optionally, add the remaining water. If using, pour in the remaining 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons of water. If you’re not accustomed to baking high-hydration loaves, omit this last addition of water the first time you try this recipe.
Finish kneading the dough. Start the mixer on low, and, to avoid splashing if you’ve added more water, gradually increase the speed to high.

Continue kneading on high speed until the dough is smooth and shiny, gathers around the dough hook, and pulls away from the sides of the mixing bowl, 10 to 20 minutes. If the dough is not ready after 10 minutes, stop the mixer for 5 minutes before continuing, to give the mixer and the dough a rest.
The dough should pass the windowpane test: grab a piece of the dough and stretch it. If the dough stretches thin enough that you can see light through it, the dough is sufficiently developed.
Rest the dough. Transfer the dough into a large bowl lightly greased with olive oil. Cover with plastic wrap and set in a warm spot in your kitchen for 30 minutes.

Stretch and fold the dough. Wet your hands and fold the dough. Starting on the side of the bowl opposite to you, scoop your fingers under the dough, stretch it up, then fold it towards you over the top of the bowl. Rotate the bowl a quarter turn, and repeat.

Repeat this twice more to complete a full rotation around the bowl. Cover the bowl, and let the dough rest 30 minutes longer. Repeat this process two more times, resting the dough for 30 minutes each time.

Finish first rise. After the third set of stretch and folds, allow the dough to rise for 1 ½ hours longer. The dough should have at least doubled in bulk, have a slightly domed top, and have visible bubbles.

Divide the dough. Set two pieces of parchment paper next to your work surface. Dust your work surface heavily with flour. Gently turn the dough out onto the counter, being careful not to deflate the dough. Sprinkle the top of the dough generously with flour.

Wet a bench knife, or other sharp knife with water. Divide the dough into 4 pieces, separating the dough after each cut so it doesn’t stick back together. Use the bench scraper and your hand to place two pieces of dough on each sheet of parchment paper, leaving space between the loaves.

Proof. Allow the loaves to rest, uncovered, at room temperature, for 1 ½ hours. An hour before baking, place a baking stone on a rack positioned in the bottom third of the oven and preheat it to 475°F (245°C).

Bake. Use an upside-down baking sheet or a pizza peel, carefully slide one of the parchment pieces with two loaves onto the preheated baking stone. Bake the loaves for 20 minutes. After 20 minutes, flip the loaves to crisp and brown the undersides.
Bake for a further 5 to 10 minutes, until deeply browned. Remove the loaves from the oven and leave them to cool on a wire rack. Repeat with the remaining 2 loaves.
Cool and serve. Leave the loaves to cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing and serving. The crust should be thin and crisp and the crumb should be soft with large air pockets.

items.name: Slow Cooked Rosemary Lamb Ragu
ingredients: 1.25 kg / 2.5 lb boneless lamb shoulder , excess fat trimmed and cut into 3 equal pieces (Note 1)
1 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (half for table salt, +50% for flakes)
2 celery sticks , grated using a box grater (discard stringy bits)
1 large carrot , peeled, grated with box grater
1 tbsp rosemary , finely chopped (substitute 2 tsp dried)
5 x 10cm/4" sprigs rosemary (sub 1 ½ tsp dried)
2 bay leaves , preferably fresh else dried
1 ½ cups red wine , full bodied (like merlot, cabernet sauvignon), or any red not too sweet or woody (substitute 0% wine or more chicken stock for non alcoholic)
1 ½ cups chicken stock/broth , low sodium
2 beef stock cubes , crumbled (I use OXO, crumbles perfectly)
¾ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (half for table salt, +50% for flakes)
500g / 1 lb pappardelle, mafaldine, rigatoni, capunti paesani or other shapes with shredded meat catching abilities! (Note 2)
1 tbsp cooking salt / kosher salt , for pasta cooking water
steps: Brown lamb, cook soffrito slowly, cook off tomato paste, deglaze and reduce wine. Slow cook lamb in sauce 2 hrs, remove, shred, simmer 30 min to reduce. Toss with cooked pasta!

Brown lamb – Sprinkle lamb with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat. Brown 2 pieces of the lamb until deep golden on both sides, about 2 – 3 minutes per side. Remove into a bowl and repeat with the 3rd piece, adding more oil if needed, then remove.

Soffrito – Lower heat to medium, cool the pot a bit if it's very hot and scrape out any loose black bits (pepper, lamb bits) but leave any tasty lamb fat in there. Add a bit of oil if your pot is looking a bit dry. Then add the onion, celery, carrot, garlic and rosemary. Cook slowly for 7 – 8 minutes until softened but don't let them colour. Don't rush this step, it's key for good ragu flavour.

Deglaze and reduce wine – Turn heat up to high and add the tomato paste. Stir for 1 ½ minutes to cook out the sourness and deepen the colour from red to brown. Then add the wine and simmer rapidly, scraping the base of the pot, until reduced by half.

Slow cook – Add tomato, stock, 3 rosemary sprigs, bay leaves, crumbled stock cubes, salt and pepper. Mix, add lamb (and any juices in the bowl) and let it come to a simmer. Then put the lid on and reduce the heat to low or medium low so it's simmering very gently. Slow cook for 2 hours or until the lamb is tender enough to shred. (Note 3 for other cook methods)
Shred – Remove lamb and shred using two forks. Cut excessively long strands using scissors. (Keep the pot on stove on medium heat without the lid while you do this).

Reduce sauce – Remove and discard rosemary and bay leaves. Return lamb into sauce and add the remaining 2 rosemary sprigs. Toss, then simmer on medium low for 30 minutes with the lid off, stirring every now and then, until the sauce has reduced and is thickened. Taste, and add more salt if needed. Cover and keep warm while you cook the pasta.
Cook pasta – Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the salt. Add the pasta and cook per the packet directions minus 1 minute (so it's a little underdone, it will finish cooking in the ragu).
Reserve water – Just before draining, scoop out a mugful of the cloudy pasta water. Drain pasta.
Toss – Return pasta into the pasta cooking pot with 6 – 7 cups (1.2 – 1.4kg) of the warm ragu (start with 6, add another cup if you want). Set the pot over medium high heat.

If your ragu was very thick rather than saucy (it thickens the longer it is sitting around), add ¼ to ⅓ cup pasta cooking water. Then toss with spatulas until the meat is tangled through the pasta and all the pasta is stained red, there should be no sauce pooled in the bottom of the pot.
If at anytime the pasta gets too stiff and sticky, just add more pasta cooking water.

Serve – Divide between warmed pasta bowls or pour into a large serving bowl and let everyone help themselves with parmesan on the side! Add a side of Garlic Bread and a fresh Balsamic Rocket Salad on the side and finish with a beautiful Tiramisu. 🙂

items.name: Baked Apples Recipe
ingredients: 2 tbsp all purpose or gluten-free flour
steps: Preheat oven to 350ºF.
Cut apples in half and remove core and seeds with a small pairing knife or spoon.
In a small bowl combine butter, brown sugar, flour, oats and cinnamon. Spoon on top of the apple halves and sprinkle with cinnamon.

Place on a cookie sheet and bake in the oven for 30 to 35 minutes, depending on the size of the apple. The apples are ready when a paring knife slides easily into the flesh and the oat topping is golden.
Serve warm with a scoop of ice cream, if desired.

items.name: 19 Healthy Ground Beef Recipes You'll Come Back To
Spiced Beef Baked Potatoes
ingredients: 4 large russet potatoes (about 10 oz. each), scrubbed, patted dry
2¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided, plus more
1 medium red or yellow onion, finely chopped
¼ cup sliced pimiento-stuffed green olives
steps: Place racks in middle and lower third of oven; preheat to 425°. Prick 4 large russet potatoes (about 10 oz. each), scrubbed, patted dry, all over with a fork, then rub all over with 1 Tbsp. vegetable oil and sprinkle with 1¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Place a baking sheet in oven on bottom rack to catch any drips, then arrange potatoes directly on middle rack and bake until skins are crisp and flesh is very soft, (an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should register 212°–220°), 55–75 minutes.
(If thermometer registers 210° before beef mixture is finished, turn off oven and leave potatoes inside until ready to use.).

Meanwhile, pick enough leaves from ½ bunch cilantro (about 2 oz.) to measure ½ cup; set aside for serving. Finely chop remaining leaves and all of stems (you should have about ¾ cup); set aside separately.

Heat remaining 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium. Add 1 medium red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 5 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is softened, 8–10 minutes.
Add ¼ cup double-concentrated tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, until deepened in color and slightly tacky, about 2 minutes.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add 1 lb. ground beef, 2 Tbsp. chili powder, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Cook, stirring and smashing often with a heatproof rubber spatula to break up meat, until cooked through, about 4 minutes.

Reduce heat to low. Add ½ cup golden raisins, ¼ cup sliced pimiento-stuffed green olives, reserved chopped cilantro, and 1 cup water. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly and flavors come together, 8–12 minutes. Taste beef mixture and season with more salt if needed. Remove from heat and cover. Let sit until ready to use.

Transfer potatoes to a platter or plates and let cool 5 minutes. Using a fork, prick a 3"–4"-long line in the center down length of each potato, leaving 1" unpricked on each end. Using your hands, firmly press ends down toward platter to split potatoes open. Smash flesh as desired, then season inside of potatoes with salt. Divide beef mixture among potatoes and top with reserved cilantro leaves.

items.name: Onion Tart
ingredients: ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt plus additional for serving
6 to 8 sprigs fresh thyme plus fresh leaves for serving
1 sheet frozen puff pastry thawed according to package directions
1 large egg beaten with 1 teaspoon water to create an egg wash
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Peel the onions, then slice them crosswise ¼-inch thick through the equator (not the ends) so that you create rings. I HIGHLY recommend a mandoline for easy, even slicing. Try to keep the layers in each slice together so you have onion "discs."
Create 6 drizzle patches of olive oil spaced evenly over the parchment in 2 rows of 3 (see video for suggested placement).
Drizzle the honey over the oil, then sprinkle each patch with a pinch of flaky salt and black pepper. Lay a small thyme sprig across each one.
Find your largest onion discs and lay one over each patch. Then, take the smaller discs and fill in the gaps. Almost no parchment should peek through; a little overlap is fine.
Lay the Gruyère slices over the onions, spacing them evenly and leaving a border of at least 1 inch on all sides.

Unfold the puff pastry on a lightly floured work surface. Roll it into a rectangle about 2 inches longer than the onions on each side (mine was 10 by 13). Gently drape the pastry over the onions. With the tines of a fork, press the edges of the pastry all the way around to create a border.
Brush the pastry lightly with the egg wash. Dab up any pools that collect with a paper towel.
Bake the onion tart for 25 to 30 minutes on the center rack, until the pastry is deeply golden and puffed.

Let rest 5 to 10 minutes. Set a large cutting board on top of the pan. Working quickly and confidently, flip the board and tart over together so the tart is now sitting on the board. Lift off the pan and peel away the parchment. Drizzle with balsamic glaze, scatter with fresh thyme leaves and flaky salt, and slice into squares.

items.name: 29 Green Bean Recipes That’ll Make Other Veggies Envious
Bacon-Wrapped Pork Tenderloin with Delicata Squash and Pear
ingredients: 2 tablespoons whole-grain mustard (divided (check label for GF))
2 delicata squash (about 14 oz each, seeded and cut ½-inch thick)
1 large Bartlett pear (ripe, about 8 ounces, cored and cut into 8 wedges (about ¾-inch thick))
1 small red onion (about 8 ounces, cut into 16 wedges (about ½-inch thick))
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Spray a large sheet pan with oil. Adjust the center rack and the top rack 6 inches from the heating element.
Season pork with 1 teaspoon salt and 1 tablespoon mustard. Lay the bacon halves on a cutting board next to each other.
Carefully lay the tenderloin over the bacon. Tightly roll up the pork jelly-roll style. Tie the roast at 2- inch intervals with kitchen string each about 12-inches long to keep the bacon on the pork.
In a large bowl, toss together the delicata squash, Bartlett pear, red onion, olive oil, maple syrup, 1 tablespoon whole grain mustard and 1 teaspoons salt.
Place the pork tenderloin in the center of the sheet pan then arrange the vegetables and pears around the pork.
Roast in the oven until the center of the thickest piece of pork reaches 145°F with a meat thermometer and the vegetables and pears are tender, about 25 minutes.
Broil on the upper rack about 5 minutes, to brown the bacon and caramelize the vegetables (careful not to burn).
Remove from the oven and let it rest 5 minutes. Slice the pork against the grain into 12 slices then divide the vegetables and pear wedges among 4 plates.

items.name: Savory Pumpkin Fritters
ingredients: ¼ cup Parmesan cheese finely grated,
¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
steps: Gather and prep all ingredients.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the pumpkin and egg until smooth.

Add the flour, Parmesan, baking powder, garlic powder, onion, parsley, poultry seasoning, salt, pepper, and Dijon. Stir until the mixture forms a thick, spoonable batter. If it feels too loose, add extra flour 1 tablespoon at a time.
Heat the vegetable oil in a medium non-stick skillet over medium heat until oil is shimmering and about 350°F.
Scoop heaping tablespoons of batter into the hot oil and gently flatten each one with the back of a spoon.
Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crisp.
Transfer the fritters to a paper towel–lined plate. Sprinkle them with a little parsley and a tiny pinch of salt while they’re still hot.
In a small bowl, stir together all dipping sauce ingredients. Serve the warm fritters with the garlic herb sauce and enjoy!

items.name: Creamy Sausage Italian Soup
ingredients: 500g/ 1 lb potato gnocchi , preferably from fridge rather than aisle (tastes better! Note 1) – or homemade Ricotta Gnocchi
500g/ 1 lb Italian pork sausage meat (homemade or store-bought) or good sausages with meat removed from casings (Note 2)
¾ tsp Italian herb mix (just the standard mix from grocery stores)
¼ tsp red chilli flakes (red pepper flakes), optional
2 celery sticks , cut into small pieces (think – soup spoon eating size)
1 large carrot , peeled and cut into small pieces
⅓ cup Chardonnay or other dry white wine, substitute water (for non-alcoholic)
4 cups (1 litre) chicken stock/broth , low sodium
½ tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, +50% for flakes)
½ cup parmesan , finely grated, plus more for serving
1 ½ cups baby spinach , or torn kale leaves
steps: Brown sausage, remove. Cook onion and garlic, then carrot, celery, herbs and chilli flakes for 2 min. Deglaze with wine. Stir in flour, then stock, salt, pepper and sausage. Simmer 5 min. Add cream, simmer 5 min. Add gnocchi and parmesan, simmer 2 min (or per packet). Stir in spinach, serve.

Heat oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up as you go, until browned. Remove with a slotted spoon into a bowl, leaving the fat in the pot. (If the pot looks dry, add a bit more oil)
Sauté – Lower the heat to medium high. Add the onion and garlic, cook for 2 minutes. Then add the carrot, celery, Italian herb mix and chilli flakes, and stir for another 2 minutes.
Deglaze with wine – Add the wine and let it simmer until mostly evaporated.

Make broth – Stir in the flour, it will form a light paste coating everything. Add half the stock and stir to dissolve the paste into the liquid, it will turn a milky colour. Add the remaining stock, salt and pepper. Then add the sausage along with any juices pooled in the bowl.

Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring every now and then. Add cream, simmer for another 5 minutes, stirring once in a while. Add parmesan and gnocchi, stir, simmer for 2 minutes (or whatever time is on the gnocchi packet).
Stir in spinach, then ladle into bowls and serve with a sprinkle of parmesan. Crusty bread for dunking feels essential for this one. 🙂

items.name: Cacio e Pepe Peas
ingredients: ¾ teaspoon black pepper (freshly coarsely ground, plus more for serving)
½ cup Pecorino Romano (finely grated, plus more for serving if desired)
2 tablespoons water (room-temperature, plus more as needed)
steps: Stir the Pecorino and 2 tablespoons water together in a small bowl to make a thick paste.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the black pepper and stir for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the frozen peas and cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 4 to 5 minutes. If there’s excess liquid in the pan, let it cook off.

Remove the skillet from the heat and let it stand for 30 seconds. Add the Pecorino mixture and toss until the peas are coated, adding another tablespoon of water if needed. Finish with grated cheese and black pepper.

items.name: Crockpot Mac and Cheese
ingredients: 12 oz. sharp cheddar cheese freshly shredded, (3 cups) $2.69**
4 oz. cream cheese cut into small pieces,
½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
steps: Gather all of the ingredients and grease a 6-quart slow cooker with nonstick spray or a little oil or butter.
Shred the cheddar cheese using the large holes of a box grater.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the macaroni and cook for 4 minutes. Drain well.****
Transfer the drained macaroni to the prepared slow cooker and toss with the butter until the pasta is evenly coated.
Add the evaporated milk, whole milk, shredded cheddar, cream cheese, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, black pepper, and salt. Stir well to combine.

Cover and cook on LOW for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring every 20 minutes, until the macaroni is tender and the cheese is melted and creamy. If the macaroni looks dry while cooking, stir in a splash of whole milk.
Switch the slow cooker to WARM and serve. If the mac and cheese thickens while sitting, stir in a splash of whole milk to loosen the sauce.

items.name: Turkish Pasta (Yoğurtlu, Kıymalı Makarna)
ingredients: 1 medium green bell pepper, finely diced
1 pound conchiglie or another pasta of your choice (gluten-free, if preferred)
1 8-ounce can tomato sauce or 1 cup chopped, canned tomatoes
1 small bunch flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
steps: Make the Garlic Yogurt. Take the yogurt out of the refrigerator and place in a bowl. Roughly chop garlic, add a pinch of salt, and continue to chop together until finely minced. Stir the garlic into the yogurt, then taste and adjust the seasoning, if needed. Cover and set aside at room temperature.
Make the Spiced Oil. Pour the olive oil into a pan, place over a low-medium heat, stir in the Aleppo pepper and dried mint and gently infuse for 35 to 40 seconds. Set aside to cool.

Sauté the vegetables. Pour the olive oil into a wide heavy pan and place over a medium-high heat. Stir in the onion and sauté for 5 minutes, then stir in the carrot and pepper and sauté for a further 2 to 3 minutes, until somewhat softened. Add the ground meat and garlic and sauté for 4 to 5 minutes until the meat is browned, stirring continuously.

Make the sauce. Add the tomato paste, tomato sauce, and water, swirling a little of the water in the can to get any remaining bits of tomato. Season with cumin, and a pinch (about ½ teaspoon each) salt and black pepper.

Stir to combine and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Taste for seasoning and add more salt or black pepper, if needed. Stir in a handful of chopped fresh parsley and turn off the heat.

Cook the pasta. About 10 minutes before the meat sauce is done cooking, bring a pan of salted water to the boil, then add the pasta and cook according to the package instructions. Drain the pasta, then divide it amongst your serving bowls.

Finish and serve. Ladle the meat sauce over the pasta then top with cherry tomatoes. Dollop with the garlic yogurt. Drizzle with the spiced olive oil, scatter with more fresh parsley, and serve immediately.

items.name: Buffalo Chicken Pasta
ingredients: 1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs cut into ½-inch pieces
4 ounces cream cheese or Neufchâtel cut into chunks and softened to room temperature
¼ cup Buffalo sauce such as Frank’s RedHot, plus additional for serving
3 ounces shredded mozzarella about ⅔ cup*
2 ounces shredded sharp cheddar about ¼ cup*
steps: In a medium bowl, toss the chicken with the garlic powder, onion powder, dill, cayenne, and salt until evenly coated.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Once it's hot, add the butter and let melt. Add the chicken in a single layer and brown on all sides until golden, about 4 minutes. (It does not need to be cooked through.)
Add the tomatoes with their liquid, broth, and pasta. Stir, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Cover and bring to a simmer. (The pasta won't be fully submerged). Once simmering, uncover and stir, then replace the lid and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Simmer 10 to 12 minutes, uncovering to stir every 3 to 4 minutes then covering again, until the pasta is al dente.
Turn off the heat. Add the Buffalo sauce and cream cheese, stirring until smooth.

Add the mozzarella and cheddar a handful at a time, stirring until each addition melts before adding the next (do not add it too quickly, or the cheese may lump). Taste and adjust the seasoning as desired.
Serve hot, topped with green onions and an additional drizzle of Buffalo sauce to taste.

items.name: Greek Chicken Soup
ingredients: ½ cup long grain white rice uncooked, $0.19***
1 large lemon juiced, (¼ cup lemon juice)
½ tsp salt or to taste,
¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
steps: Gather all ingredients.
Dice onion and celery, slice carrots into halfmoons, and mince garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery and garlic. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have softened.

Add the chicken breast, chicken broth, rice, dried dill, salt, and pepper. Increase the heat to medium high and bring the soup to a boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board. Shred it into bite-sized pieces using two forks.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs and lemon juice until smooth.
Slowly ladle 1 cup of the hot broth into the egg mixture while whisking constantly. Repeat with a second cup of broth, continuing to whisk until fully incorporated.

Reduce the heat to low. Return the shredded chicken to the pot, add the parsley, then slowly pour in the tempered egg mixture while stirring constantly. Cook just until the soup is warmed through and slightly creamy, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Let the soup cool for a few minutes, then serve warm with additional parsley and crusty bread, if desired.

items.name: 7 Day High Protein Diet Meal Plan
Pumpkin Curry
ingredients: 1 pie pumpkin seeds removed, skin removed & small dice, (about 2 lbs., 4 cups) $2.62*
1 cup long grain white rice uncooked,
½ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
13.66 oz. can full-fat unsweetened coconut milk
15 oz. can 100% pumpkin puree not pumpkin pie filling, $1.96***
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients. Using a chef’s knife, carefully cut the pie pumpkin in half from top to bottom, starting right beside the stem. Use a spoon to scoop out the seeds and stringy pulp. (Save the seeds for roasting, if you'd like!)

Cut away the stem and the small piece of the bottom. Place the pumpkin halves cut-side down, then cut each half into ½"-wide wedges. Then, using your knife, remove the skin from each wedge and dice into small cubes. Continue until all of the pumpkin is diced.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, add the cubed pumpkin and onions in an even layer. Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the pumpkin and onions are cooking, you can start the rice. Add the rice and water to a medium pot and cook it according to the package instructions. Set aside when finished.
After the pumpkin and onions have cooked for about 10 minutes, add the garlic and ginger and sauté for 1-2 minutes until aromatic.
Next, add the tomato paste and continue cooking for another 1-2 minutes.
Sprinkle in the garam masala, curry powder, cumin, salt, and pepper, and stir to combine.
Pour in the coconut milk and pumpkin puree. Stir to combine. Bring the curry to a simmer and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Then, stir in the brown sugar until dissolved.
Lastly, pour in the vegetable broth and stir to combine. Taste and adjust for seasoning and texture. Feel free to add an additional splash of broth.
Serve the pumpkin curry over the rice with desired toppings, then enjoy!

items.name: Maple Dijon Sheet Pan Chicken
ingredients: 2 tablespoons maple syrup (I used Wholesome Yum sugar-free maple syrup)
1 ½ pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs, (cut into cubes)
12 ounces butternut squash (cut into ¾-inch cubes)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F and spray a large rimmed baking sheet with oil. Line it with foil first, if desired.

Add the mustard, maple syrup, olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, dried parsley, and red pepper flakes to a large mixing bowl. Whisk until evenly combined.
Add the chicken, Brussels sprouts, and butternut squash and toss until everything is evenly coated.

Transfer the mixture to the prepared sheet pan and spread it into an even layer. Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Broil for an additional 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely, for a little extra char, if desired.
Serve with a salad or a grain, such as wild rice, brown rice, or a brown rice and quinoa blend.
